html:
One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever to reach land. It struck the central Philippines on 8 November 2013 and killed more than 6,000 people.

Filipinos called it Yolanda. It crossed the islands of the Visayas, including Samar, Leyte and Panay, with winds among the highest ever measured at landfall. The deadliest blow was a storm surge several metres high that swept into Tacloban, a city of over 200,000 on a narrow bay. Many people had sheltered in buildings near the shore and drowned there. Millions lost their homes.

Aid poured in from around the world, but roads, airports and phones were down, and relief was slow to reach many towns.

The storm came as world leaders met for climate talks in Warsaw. A Philippine delegate began a fast there until the meeting agreed real action, and Haiyan became a symbol of what warming seas may bring to poor, low lying countries. It was one of a string of deadly storms in the region, after Cyclone Nargis in Burma, and it raised questions about climate change.
sum: One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever to reach land. It struck the central Philippines on 8 November 2013 and killed more than 6,000 people.
